gen_risks.description: Incomplete needs assessment and inadequate geotechnical studies may cause design changes, leading to time and cost overruns.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct thorough design reviews, include contingency budgets, engage experienced consultants, and enforce strict change‑control procedures.
gen_risks.evidence: Incomplete needs assessment and inadequate attention to geotechnical studies ... resulting in design changes/variations during construction and consequently time and cost overruns.

gen_risks.description: Limited domestic contracting capacity could delay works and increase costs, requiring reliance on international firms.
gen_risks.mitigation: Perform market sounding, allow joint‑venture bids, and provide capacity‑building for local firms.
gen_risks.evidence: Limited domestic contracting capacity to conduct projects of this nature, complexity, and scope; most contracts will be done by international firms.

gen_risks.description: Extreme temperature and precipitation variability may cause floods that damage water infrastructure.
gen_risks.mitigation: Integrate climate‑resilient designs, flood protection, buffer zones and early‑warning systems into all infrastructure.
gen_risks.evidence: Extreme temperature will likely trigger increased evapotranspiration and precipitation variability, leading to floods that can damage infrastructure.

gen_risks.description: Dry‑season flows at the Namatala intake may be insufficient, threatening water supply and environmental flow requirements.
gen_risks.mitigation: Complete the Augmented Water Supply Study and consider storage or alternative sources to guarantee minimum environmental flow.
gen_risks.evidence: Namatala’s dry weather flows ... may not be sufficient to meet projected water demand and maintain an adequate EF.

gen_risks.description: UWAs can meet O&M costs but lack revenue for capital investments, risking service gaps.
gen_risks.mitigation: Set up a revolving fund, adjust tariffs for full cost recovery, and secure additional donor financing for capital works.
gen_risks.evidence: UWAs can cover their routine O&M costs, but they do not generate enough revenue to cover capital investments.

gen_risks.description: Debt service on the IDA loan could strain NWSC cash flow.
gen_risks.mitigation: Phase debt service, align repayments with cash‑flow forecasts, and keep a reserve fund for contingencies.
gen_risks.evidence: Annual payments of principal and service charge would correspond to less than 1.4% of total revenues after 2025.

gen_risks.description: IFMS project module not operational may cause financial reporting errors.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prioritise full activation of the IFMS project module, train finance staff and apply manual cross‑checks during transition.
gen_risks.evidence: Project module of the IFMS is not yet fully operational ... increases the risk of errors and inaccuracy of financial reports.

gen_risks.description: PDU staff lack procurement experience and are over‑burdened, leading to procurement delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit procurement consultants, provide targeted World Bank procurement training, and augment PDU staffing.
gen_risks.evidence: PDU staff have no experience in using World Bank Procurement Regulations and have a heavy workload; leads to delays.

gen_risks.description: Delays in preparing specifications and Terms of Reference may postpone tendering.
gen_risks.mitigation: Assign a dedicated technical team to draft specifications early and use standard templates for ToRs.
gen_risks.evidence: Delays in preparing specifications, statement of requirements, and ToR by the User Departments.

gen_risks.description: Large refugee influx puts excessive pressure on water resources and public services.
gen_risks.mitigation: Coordinate with UNHCR/OPM to integrate refugee water needs, expand supply capacity and develop a refugee water tariff.
gen_risks.evidence: Estimated one million South Sudanese refugees have already migrated to Uganda, placing excessive pressure on Uganda’s public services and natural resources.

gen_risks.description: Long water‑collection distances expose women and girls to gender‑based violence.
gen_risks.mitigation: Install piped water points nearer households, ensure gender‑segregated facilities and conduct GBV awareness/training.
gen_risks.evidence: Women and girls bear the heaviest burden for water collection; long walks trigger GBV such as sexual assaults.

gen_risks.description: Complex coordination among many agencies may cause implementation delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Create a formal inter‑agency coordination framework with regular meetings and clear roles for WESLD and focal points.
gen_risks.evidence: Given the number of departments ... the MWE’s WESLD will take the responsibility for overall coordination and communication.

gen_risks.description: Regional instability from the South‑Sudan conflict could disrupt project financing and operations.
gen_risks.mitigation: Monitor regional security, develop contingency plans and maintain dialogue with donors to adjust implementation as needed.
gen_risks.evidence: The most critical risk to this outlook is regional instability, particularly from the ongoing conflict in South Sudan.

gen_risks.description: Handling of asbestos‑cement pipes poses health and environmental hazards.
gen_risks.mitigation: Follow NEMA asbestos‑handling guidelines, embed safe removal/disposal procedures in contracts and train workers on hazardous‑material safety.
gen_risks.evidence: Management measures for the removal, packaging, transportation and disposal of existing asbestos waste, following additional guidance that will be provided by NEMA.

gen_risks.description: Turnover of qualified staff reduces institutional memory and capacity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Introduce staff‑retention incentives, succession planning and knowledge‑management systems.
gen_risks.evidence: Turnover of qualified and experienced staff is noticed.

gen_risks.description: Internal audit reports are not regularly shared with the World Bank, limiting oversight.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish a schedule for timely sharing of internal‑audit reports with the World Bank and assign a liaison officer.
gen_risks.evidence: Ministry internal audit review reports are not shared regularly with the World Bank.

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risk: as detailed in the CPF, significant political uncertainty is not foreseen, but governance and effective public-sector management present substantial risks.
gt_risks.mitigation: The Project will mitigate these risks through (a) strengthening the MWE's regulatory framework; (b) carrying out a citizen engagement strategy; and (c) strengthening project implementation efforts in close coordination with local government officials and development partners. The World Bank's procurement processes will also help safeguard the Project from corruption.

gt_risks.description: Institutional capacity for implementation and sustainability risk: the Umbrella Water Authority (UWA) as a regional service delivery model for small towns and RGCs was recently introduced. Although the decision to scale up this model was informed by extensive analytical work and a pilot project, the UWA model was only recently operationalized.
gt_risks.mitigation: The Project will support implementation of a professionalized monitoring system focused on enhancing revenue collection approaches (billing software, cashless/mobile payment systems) and on strengthening integration of specialized private operators through improved contract management. The implementation team will use the Utility Performance Monitoring and Information System (UPMIS) tool to regularly review UWA and NWSC performance.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk: the Procurement risk is rated Substantial while the FM risk is Moderate. The risks identified relate to delays and skills gaps at different stages of procurement processing.
gt_risks.mitigation: IWMDP will benefit from the lessons learned and mechanisms put in place under the predecessor project (WMDP); detailed mitigation measures for the procurement risk are set out in the Appraisal (Procurement) section.

gt_risks.description: The environmental and social risk is deemed Substantial given (a) potential opposition to the introduction of a new service delivery model, including new tariffs and catchment management measures; (b) the influx of new workers in small towns and RGCs; and (c) potentially adverse environmental impacts from the construction and operation of the proposed investments.
gt_risks.mitigation: The environmental and social risk will be managed through the application of an Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF), a Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF), and related safeguards instruments (Environmental and Social Impact Assessment, Resettlement Action Plans).

gt_risks.description: Other risks (social tensions in districts hosting refugees): tensions between refugees and citizens are caused by inequity in access to and payment for water supply and sanitation (WSS) services. While refugees in the settlements benefit from humanitarian aid and GoU support, Ugandans in host communities receive limited support for services and infrastructure, causing social tension that may result in Project implementation delays given potential community opposition to the works.
gt_risks.mitigation: The GoU has prioritized development efforts for poor districts hosting refugees while remaining firmly committed to its policy on refugee protection. The Project will manage this risk by designing WSS facilities and catchment management measures that benefit both host communities and refugees, and by ensuring the Project's social and communication management plan is applied and adequately supervised. There are no known existing risks to the refugee protection framework or reputational risks for the Project.
